findings.claim: The Library of Congress Classification (LCC) places QD415-QD436 'Biochemistry' inside QD241-QD441 'Organic chemistry', itself inside QD1-QD999 'Chemistry'. The full hierarchical label returned by id.loc.gov is 'Science--Chemistry--Organic chemistry--Biochemistry'.

The Universal Decimal Classification (UDC) places class 577 'Material bases of life. Biochemistry. Molecular biology. Biophysics' directly under class 57 'Biological sciences in general', not under class 54 (Chemistry). The UDC thus files biochemistry firmly within biology, not chemistry.
findings.quote: 577 Material bases of life. Biochemistry. Molecular biology. Biophysics

findings.claim: Britannica's structured breadcrumb JSON-LD categorises the biochemistry article under Science > Biology > Branches of Biology, not under Chemistry. The article definition also explicitly frames biochemistry as the study of processes that occur in living organisms, drawing on chemistry as a tool.
findings.quote: {"@type": "BreadcrumbList", "itemListElement": [{"name": "Science"}, {"name": "Biology"}, {"name": "Branches of Biology"}]} ... "Biochemistry is the study of the chemical substances and processes that occur in plants, animals, and microorganisms and of the changes they undergo during development and life."

findings.claim: Wikidata Q7094 (Biochemistry) simultaneously asserts: P31 (instance of) = Q1665984 'interdisciplinary science', Q11790203 'branch of chemistry', and Q28598684 'branch of biology'; P279 (subclass of) = Q420 'biology' and Q11351 'organic chemistry'; P361 (part of) = Q2329 'chemistry' and Q420 'biology'. No single parent is privileged.
findings.quote: P31: [Q1665984 (interdisciplinary science), Q11790203 (branch of chemistry), Q28598684 (branch of biology)] ... P279: [Q420 (biology), Q11351 (organic chemistry)] ... P361: [Q2329 (chemistry), Q420 (biology)]

findings.claim: ASBMB, the primary North American professional society for biochemistry, describes its community as 'molecular life scientists' and frames its mission as advancing 'the molecular nature of life processes', positioning biochemistry within the life-science orbit rather than chemistry.
findings.quote: The American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB) is a nonprofit professional society that builds and empowers a broad community of molecular life scientists to advance discovery. ... ASBMB's mission is to advance the science of biochemistry and molecular biology and to promote the understanding of the molecular nature of life processes.

findings.claim: The University of Wisconsin–Madison Department of Biochemistry is housed in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences, not in a chemistry college. The homepage title reads 'Department of Biochemistry — College of Agricultural and Life Sciences — UW–Madison', providing direct institutional evidence of a life-science rather than chemistry home.
findings.quote: Department of Biochemistry – College of Agricultural and Life Sciences – UW–Madison

findings.claim: MIT lists 'Biochemistry, Biophysics, and Structural Biology' as a research area within its Department of Biology (not Chemistry). The page is hosted under biology.mit.edu and explicitly enumerates biochemistry alongside other biology research areas such as Cancer Biology, Cell Biology, and Neurobiology.
findings.quote: Areas of Research Biochemistry, Biophysics, and Structural Biology Cancer Biology Cell Biology Computational Biology Genetics Human Disease Immunology Microbiology Neurobiology Stem Cell and Developmental Biology

notes: Five independent sources (UDC 577, Britannica breadcrumb, Wikidata P31/P279/P361, ASBMB self-description, UW-Madison and MIT institutional housing) all file or frame biochemistry on the biology/life-sciences side, not under chemistry alone. Only LCC (QD415-QD436 inside Organic chemistry class QD) supports the current field:chemistry placement. Wikidata explicitly tags biochemistry as BOTH branch of chemistry and branch of biology AND as an interdisciplinary science — a textbook interface case. The LCC is the one major library classification that nests it under chemistry; UDC takes the opposite position. Institutionally, departments almost universally sit in life-science/medical schools (UW-Madison CALS, MIT Biology, Stanford Medicine), not chemistry colleges. The orchestrator should consider: (a) the current field:chemistry single-home edge is at best a partial view supported only by LCC; (b) a dual part_of to both field:chemistry and domain:life-sciences (or when a field:biology node exists) appears well-warranted by the balance of evidence; (c) Wikidata's 'interdisciplinary science' label supports an interface reading. The Springer Biochemistry (Moscow) aims page is context: it covers biochemistry alongside molecular biology, bioorganic chemistry, microbiology, immunology, physiology, and biomedical sciences — supporting the broad life-science framing rather than a narrow chemistry one.
